memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'No, my lord,' they answered. 'Your servants have come to buy food. We are all the sons of one man. Your servants are honest men, not spies.' 'No!' he said to them. 'You have come to see where our land is unprotected.' But they replied, 'Your servants were twelve brothers, the sons of one man, who lives in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.'" - Gen 42:10-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the brothers defend themselves, they mention their family, and in doing so they let slip a haunting phrase: "one is no more." They are speaking, of course, about Joseph — the brother they believe is dead, the brother standing right in front of them. They think he is gone forever, when in fact he is alive and listening to every word.

Imagine what it was like for Joseph to hear those words: "one is no more." His own brothers, unaware, were reciting the story of his supposed death — a death they had caused. The phrase reveals that the memory of what they did still lingered in the family, an unspoken wound that would not heal.

The words "one is no more" carry a heavy weight. There is often a person, a loss, a wound in a family's story that everyone circles around but no one fully faces. Buried griefs and unspoken guilts have a way of shaping a family for years, quietly present even when unmentioned.

Yet the deeper truth here is full of hope: the one they thought was "no more" was very much alive — and was, in fact, about to become their rescuer. What the brothers believed was a closed, tragic chapter, God had kept open for a purpose of salvation. Sometimes what we have written off as lost and gone, God is quietly preserving for a redemption we cannot imagine.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What buried grief or guilt quietly shapes my family's story?
2. Do I trust that God can redeem what I have written off as lost?
3. Where might God be preserving hope in a situation that feels closed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that what I think is lost and gone may be held by You for a purpose of redemption. Bring healing to the buried wounds of my family, and give me hope in what feels closed. Amen.
